💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that for over a century now, the vampire has fascinated humanity.
  • It has been revealed that in Vampire Therapist, you play undead cowboy Samuel Walls, who is invited to Germany by the three-thousand-year-old Andromachos.
  • Industry observers note that how can I help you tonight?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that for over a century now, the vampire has fascinated humanity. From books to films, television and yes, even video games, the enigma of an undead bloodsucker that nonetheless has the wisdom of the ages is a contradiction we all seek to understand. Vampire Therapist isn’t concerned with tragic backstories or merciless sadism but with how to move past them.

It has been revealed that in Vampire Therapist, you play undead cowboy Samuel Walls, who is invited to Germany by the three-thousand-year-old Andromachos. For some devious scheme? No, but to help other people. Vampires, that is. Because, as Samuel Walls, you are the one and only Vampire Therapist. And God help you, because these bloodsuckers have some problems.

Industry observers note that how can I help you tonight? Vampire Therapist is a visual novel with puzzle elements where, as Walls, your job is to - surprise, surprise - provide psychological aid to your undead kin. To do so, you listen to their problems and aim to catch them in mental contradictions which hold them back from improving or seeing reality.

It has been revealed that it can seem a little gamified, but there is definitely a fascinating deductive element to catching your client doing things like Labeling or Disqualifying the Positive, all of which seem to be real therapy terms, but which are explained in a digestible format. The focus is not on catching out your clients, but on taking advantage of these contradictions to show them where they can manage their problems.

According to recent reports, you’ll also get to make occasional decisions on what to say or do, which can shift the story in different directions. The focus is mainly on the psychological element, and that in itself is enough to carry the whole game. In fact, I was a little miffed when it got interrupted by a blood-drinking minigame, not least because it was a little janky in the build which I played.

Whenever you have an issue, you can look back at your notes to study them for references to your client’s case files, as well as Sam’s notes that point to the issues they have. You can also look up definitions of the psychological contradictions, including some handy examples. Admittedly, I missed these on my playthrough, but they are there if you’re the journal-reading type, and Andromachos will be on hand to guide you through initial sessions anyway. The Looks and Sound of Death In visual terms, Vampire Therapist is your typical visual novel. You have character sprites with occasional shifts in pose and expression, while vivid backgrounds show which scene you’re in. The art style is a decent middle ground between realistic and stylised, meaning even the more stereotypical vampires, such as the half-century-old Renaissance aristocrat, aren’t boiled down to simple caricatures.

Sources indicate that the music in Vampire Therapist is pretty simple, consisting of the main theme and occasional background noises. I did find the track that plays in the vampire club, which your patron Andromachos uses as his base of operations, a little repetitive, which can be an problem since you revisit it pretty frequently.

Recent findings suggest that the voice acting, however, is undoubtedly a standout. Naturally, Matthew Mercer provides his vocal talent as incidental character Reinhard, and also appears later on in the full game. But Cyrus Nemati is a standout as Sam Walls, who provides cosy mix of stereotypical gravely cowboy and surprisingly self-aware, world-wise wanderer. What’s the story, morning glory? The actual narrative of Vampire Therapist is pretty engaging, and what we find out about Sam Walls, Andromachos and your clients such as Doctor Drayne (yes, really) and Isabella d’Este paints a fascinating picture of vampiric history. There are definitely shades of Underworld and Vampire: The Masquerade, but Vampire Therapist stays on the lighter side of things.

Industry observers note that the motivations and backstory for your clients also manage to quite elegantly marry typical vampiric tropes with more realistic psychological conditions. Doctor Drayne struggles with addiction, only it’s to an experimental plasma he’s been making at his pharmaceutical company as part of a synthetic blood substitute.

The Contessa d’Este, meanwhile, is a literal Renaissance woman who struggles with depression and anger at the world, because after funding the great arts in her heyday, seeing Space Wars: Rise of Spacewalker (no prize for what that’s parodying) made her think all her efforts to enlighten humanity were for nought.

It has been revealed that about the only problem I had is that Vampire Therapist, for what I played at least, seems to sidestep some more pressing issues and leaves a lot of questions unanswered about character motivations. Drayne, for example, is mostly concerned that his addiction to the experimental plasma is affecting his workaholic lifestyle, but the fact he has no memory of what happens when he consumes the substance isn’t given any attention at all.

Admittedly, it’d be a bit awkward to delve into Andromachos’ backstory as the Terror of the Mediterranean, and it might well be something brought up in latter parts of the story. Still, it can feel as though there are some elements that should be explored further, especially as we do get a lot of detail about Sam Walls’ path to redemption even in the first part of Vampire Therapist. What’s been biting at you this evening? Vampire Therapist doesn’t have much in the way of challenges, as I see it. It’s a solid visual novel with an original premise, some intriguing puzzle gameplay and a genuinely fascinating, intriguing approach to explaining concepts of mental health and therapy that I found quite informative.

It has been revealed that the only problem is that it does presume a lot about the player and how they want Sam Walls to act. Especially considering one early section has Walls nibbling (consensually) on some goth necks in a very sensually implied manner. It’s not as though you’re not warned that it delves into mature topics, but if you’re like me and couldn’t stand the romance in something like Baldur’s Gate 3 it can still feel a bit awkward.

But those are small potatoes, and my earlier mention of stuff I think the story could have done better is only evidence of how much I was paying attention to, and absorbing, the world and its characters, which I think is the highest praise you can give anything narrative-based. It’s lightweight, narrow in scale and perfect for relaxing while offering something of a challenge as you learn more about your clients and try to help them ground themselves and, if not resolve, then at least manage their problems. Let’s put a stake in this What I really liked about Vampire Therapist was how it connected the complications faced by immortals to real-world mental problems without seeming hokey. It’s not just that the Contessa is feeling depressed; it’s that seeing the world go from the Mona Lisa to Rise of Skywalker has seemingly given her concrete evidence that her years of patronage to the fine arts were worthless.

This makes Vampire Therapist feel worthwhile for fans of vampire fiction, as well as those just looking for a fascinating story. Add to that the intriguing explanations of therapy terms, psychological distortions and explorations of the (in)human condition, and ironically it feels as though a game about vampires helps to demystify the idea.

If you’re looking for a solid visual novel with a bit of meat on its bones, and some great art and audio that elevates what rather bashfully calls itself a low-budget indie, then Vampire Therapist is a must-play!

I've not played it but it seems like a good take on the format. Clearly, though, sometimes you just need to play the hits, as a new release of the original game is on the way in the form of Super Meat Boy Again+, a remaster with updated graphics, levels and plenty more.

According to recent reports, what is there is very clearly Super Meat Boy, uh, again, just with a big new lick of paint. There is probably some kind of joke to be made about it being DLSS yassified, but I'm too tired to think of one, so, you get the point. But it does look pretty good! Apparently it's not just the art that's new, as there's also new music, cutscenes, secrets and "stuff.".

Sources indicate that if the animated sequences featured in the trailer, which you can have a gander at above, are included in the final game that'll be a treat to watch too, as I think they better capture the Newgrounds pseudo sub-genre of animation than the graphical overhaul. It sounds like they will be looking at the Steam page, so, a treat to look forward to while committing an act of masochism by playing it!

There's no release date attached to this remaster, so we'll all just have to sit tight for an patch there. The original is still listed on Steam, but if you fancy as substantial a dose of nostalgia as the trailer is trying to present to you, you could always go play the original, plain old regular Meat Boy. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game.
  • The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game. The twist is that the specs not only include useful information for PC players, they also cover similarly relevant details for console players, who traditionally don’t get mentioned in those reveals.

The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

In a recent development, on the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG. Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

In a recent development, with the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

That same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

It’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

According to recent reports, and, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

Crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.

10 Games to Play While Waiting for GTA VI to Go on Sale

💡 Key Takeaways
  • After 13 years, Rockstar’s long awaited follow-up to Grand Theft Auto V, Grand Theft Auto VI, has finally arrived on Xbox and PlayStation consoles to widespread critical and financial acclaim, becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history.
  • While millions of people are playing through GTA VI today, many are also holding off from playing the game until it goes on sale due its high price ranging from $80-$100 and massive file size of 212 GB, taking up a massive chunk of the base PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S internal storage.
  • For those gamers who are holding off on purchasing GTA VI until it goes on sale, here’s a list of 10 GTA VI-like titles they should check out in the meantime that are currently being sold at more affordable prices and balanced file sizes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After 13 years, Rockstar’s long awaited follow-up to Grand Theft Auto V, Grand Theft Auto VI, has finally arrived on Xbox and PlayStation consoles to widespread critical and financial acclaim, becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history.

While millions of people are playing through GTA VI today, many are also holding off from playing the game until it goes on sale due its high price ranging from $80-$100 and massive file size of 212 GB, taking up a massive chunk of the base PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S internal storage.

For those gamers who are holding off on purchasing GTA VI until it goes on sale, here’s a list of 10 GTA VI-like titles they should check out in the meantime that are currently being sold at more affordable prices and balanced file sizes.

Some people just enjoy Grand Theft Auto games for their comedy and freedom to sow chaos throughout cities and for people who enjoy that type of experience they should check out the FPS High on Life from the creators of Rick and Morty.

Here, people play as a human as they wind up being teleported to the alien metropolis of Blim City to become an intergalactic bounty hunter with living guns called Gatlians guiding them to take down the G3 Cartel that intends on turning the entire human race into drugs.

High on Life is as ridiculous and hilarious as it sounds, essentially being a perfect translation of Rick and Morty’s signature comedy style to video game form, and it will certainly give players many laughs as they wait for GTA VI to go on sale.

Ever since Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, flying all kinds of aircraft has been an integral part of the GTA experience and for those who enjoy flying more than driving in the franchise, there’s no better game to check out while waiting for GTA VI sales than Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024.

The latest entry in the long-running Microsoft Flight Simulator series, Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is the most advanced publicly available flight simulator, allowing players to learn how to fly a wide variety of aircraft in first or third-person such as airships, gliders, hot air balloons, jets, and more.

Not only that, but the game additionally allows players to fly any aircraft across the planet’s most famous natural and urban environments such as Zion National Park, Mount Fuji, London, and Miami which is what GTA VI’s Vice City is directly based on.

Even more so than flying, driving has arguably been the defining factor of the GTA franchise with the series initially starting out as a top-down driving-focused game and if GTA fans wanted to check out the most advanced realistic racing game, then they’d have to play Forza Horizon 6.

Currently an Xbox Series X|S console exclusive, Forza Horizon 6 has players journey to the rural and urban streets of a stylised version of Tokyo as they strive to qualify for the Horizon Festival or simply drive around Japan’s wondrous landscapes using over 500 cars.

There’s far more to do in Forza Horizon 6 than just driving around Japan as players can customize a massive estate filled with garages and custom tracks or players can customize public roads to use in multiplayer races.

Some people may enjoy the GTA series for the driving, flying, or comedy but oftentimes people like those games for the freedom to cause chaos in any way they desire, with one game that offers a similar style of player freedom being Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster.

An RE Engine remake of 2006’s Dead Rising, Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster follows the photojournalist Frank West as he sneaks his way into a Willamette, Colorado mall to cover a zombie outbreak only to get trapped in the mall and attempt to investigate the outbreak’s origins.

While players can stick to completing the game’s many time limited narrative cases, players can instantly go about slaying zombies and psychopaths in any way they want by using practically anything found in the mall such as jugs of orange juice, CDs, katanas, potted plants, shopping carts, and more.

If people want to experience a game with a similar story and setting to GTA VI, there are actually a few good games to choose from with one of the more underrated options being Hangar 13’s Mafia III.

Recent findings suggest that the first Mafia game to not be developed by series creator Illusion Softworks, Mafia III follows Vietnam War veteran turned crime lord Lincoln Clay in the U.S. gulf coast city of New Bordeaux as he sets out to avenge his adoptive father and brother after they were killed by the Marcano crime family.

While Mafia III isn’t set in the present day, it still features a similarly enthralling and emotional story, one that tackles social challenges of late 1960s America and features multiple different endings depending on Clay’s actions and choices during his campaign to take down the local mafia.

When it comes to video games centered around crime, most people wouldn’t consider an entry from the war-focused Battlefield series to be one but in 2015, Visceral Games did just that by creating the crime and police centered Battlefield Hardline.

Visceral’s final game ever released, Battlefield Hardline’s campaign follows Miami Police Detective Nick Mendoza attempting to take down drug dealers and suppliers in the Florida based city only to discover corruption in the MPD and wind up being framed for a crime he didn’t commit.

Hardline may not have been the game traditional Battlefield fans wanted at the time of its release but Visceral’s writing and gameplay prowess managed to make it stand as not only one of the most unique Battlefield games but also one of the most intriguing and cinematic.

Ubisoft is famous for creating immersive open-world titles like the numerous entries from the Assassin’s Creed and Far Cry series but it wasn’t until 2014 that the publisher decided to make a more grounded GTA-like experience with Watch Dogs.

Set in Chicago and the same universe as the Assassin’s Creed franchise, Watch Dogs follows hacker Aiden Pearce who, after a heist goes wrong, sets out to find the people responsible for putting a hit on him resulting in the death of his niece Lena.

What ensues is an action-packed yet stealthy gaming experience as Pearce is able to hack particularly every piece of technology in the city from cellphones to trains and construction equipment to aid him in tracking his enemies down in between instances where Pearce has to steal cars or engage in gun fights.

While Mafia III and Watch Dogs are fun GTA-like titles, neither of them compare to the pure chaos and drama that can be unleashed in CD Projekt Red’s ambitious first-person, open-world, action RPG Cyberpunk 2077.

The latest brand-new game developed by the makers of The Witcher game series, Cyberpunk 2077 has players embody the cyborg mercenary V in the futuristic and crime-filled metropolis of Night City as they get caught up in a movement to take down the corrupt Arasaka Corporation.

Cyberpunk 2077’s reputation may have been marred by a buggy 2020 launch but it has since gone on to become one of the best modern RPGs thanks to beneficial updates and its Phantom Liberty DLC making the game’s core combat, dialogue, and side activities all the more fun.

GTA VI is set in the present day but its greatest gaming influence on a technical and narrative level is undoubtedly Rockstar Games’ previous modern gaming big hit, Red Dead Redemption 2.

Set roughly 12 years before Red Dead Redemption 1 at the turn of the 20th century, Red Dead Redemption 2 primarily follows Van der Linde gang member Arthur Morgan as he and the rest of the gang struggle to survive against rival gangs, nature itself, and the ever-dominating presence of industrialized civilization.

Before GTA VI, Red Dead Redemption 2 was Rockstar’s most cinematic and immersive game ever made as not only did it feature a far more serious and emotional story than any GTA game before but it allowed players to do all kinds of things in the old west such as hunting wildlife, taking care of horses, crafting materials, and more.

For anybody still waiting on GTA VI or consoles with large internal storage capacities to go on sale, the number one game they have to play in the meantime is the multi console generational juggernaut itself, GTA V.

GTA VI is making records now but GTA V was a phenomenon all on its own for over a decade as it constantly outsold almost every other game on the market for years on end partly due to its campaign following Franklin, Michael, and Trevor in Los Santos but mainly due to its ever evolving GTA Online.

With GTA VI’s iteration of GTA Online likely months away from launch, it’ll be good to finish up whatever players haven’t done yet in GTA Online, such as its many heists and mode customization options, before everyone migrates over to GTA VI’s multiplayer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that you may have recently read that CD Projekt Red's in-development Cyberpunk 2 may be trying to revive the original game's online ambitions. But, if you don't want to wait the many years it'll likely be before the Cyberpunk 2077 sequel arrives, then I've got good news for you: Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta.

Recent findings suggest that "After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders on the CyberMP Discord channel wrote (thanks RPS). "Anyone can jump in and play now - no invites or applications needed." The team notes, however, that this is "true beta", meaning "Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers.".

Alongside the potential shakiness, the devs say it's also possible the mod could ping your anti-virus software, since it "doesn't have a digital signature yet". Whilst the priorities for the team lie in "polishing the foundations" and "fixing crashes and stability", more features are eventually planned. But for now, they stress, "let's see how the project handles real player traffic!".

In a recent development, so, what exactly is it? CyberMP is a dedicated multiplayer modification for Cyberpunk 2077 that allows you and your friends to explore Night City together: drive vehicles, engage in combat, and play custom community-created game modes on high-tick dedicated servers. You need an official copy of the game to play it (obviously), and the mod is completely free to download. You can download the mod, and read a fair amount of how to get it working, what to expect from it, and how to troubleshoot any challenges, over at its dedicated website.

Sources indicate that if you're thinking 'Hang on, why does Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer sound so familiar?', it's because the game was supposed to receive an official multiplayer mode after its original release. Thanks to its shaky launch, however, plans changed, and CD Projekt Red later unveiled that multiplayer would be a separate "triple-A release", but, eventually, that too was cancelled. The studio is still keen to honour the idea, though, and recently stated it's "focusing on bringing online into all of our franchises one day".

This isn't the first substantial bit of news we've had about Cyberpunk 2077 mods this week. Just yesterday, a latest mod called 'Torrent' added 3D rain, lightning storms, and tyre spray to Night City - all rendered and made lovely with a new lighting system that seems to play nicely with other weather mods that have been created for the game.

Battlefield 6 is getting a free trial next week with a decent selection of maps and modes

📅 13 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (563 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week.
  • Though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous.
  • Industry observers note that for starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

Though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

Industry observers note that for starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

According to recent reports, once downloaded, you’ll find a new Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

Once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the latest Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

In a recent development, all-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

Recent findings suggest that casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for new players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

It has been revealed that casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

Recent findings suggest that the most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

According to recent reports, this is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a massive new revision - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.

When you think about GTA as a series, the first thing that probably comes to mind is driving through crowds of people, gunning down whoever you like, just generally doing crime without any care in the world. I wouldn't exactly call it an empathy game, not to say that other games are any better at such a thing anyway. But with GTA 6 out, crikey, next bloody week, a new interview has gone up with co-studio head Rob Nelson where he shared that you have a bit more space to be empathetic compared to previous entries.

"Crime is a fundamental part of GTA - at least up until now, it has been," Nelson told The Guardian (via @GameRoll_, ta IGN) in a fresh interview. "We're trying to make sure we're not punishing people for playing the game they are used to … [but] your actions will have some effect on how the game plays out." When asked about whether this will be the first GTA game to encourage people to be empathetic, Nelson responded, "I would say so. I would say that it's a product of the story we're trying to tell. We've tried for the first time in a GTA to provide mechanisms that encourage it, for those who want to.".

I am deeply curious as to what those mechanics may be, given that most of what we've seen so far is pretty relegated to shootin', lootin' and a bit of smoochin'. If you steal a car, is there an NPC that loses their job because of it? Can you repair the harm you caused through that action? I'm sure hardly anyone else that's vibrating through their skin in excitement for almost having the game in their fingertips will be asking such questions, I'm just often wary of empathy mechanics in games.

Sources indicate that in any case, doesn't matter all that much for us PC lot just yet, especially because Rockstar are preparing themselves both legally and technically to tackle pirated copies of the game. Rockstar will obviously be quite busy at the moment too, not just because of that whole launching a game thing, but because UK-based workers will be voting to unionise as we speak. If formed, it could be 1600 members strong, which would make it the biggest games union in the UK. Solidarity with all the workers as the voting process continues. I hope you get the result you deserve.

At Tier 2, you’ll be able to open up to 40 Gifts a day, receive 125 Gifts from spinning Stops and get 10 extra Gift slots in your bag. Reaching Tier 3 unlocks x2 Daily Adventure Incense duration, and Tier 4 provides increased Stardust and XP from hatching Eggs.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, having the Deluxe Go Pass bolsters those Tier 2 ranks, raising those totals to 50, 150, and 20, respectively. I must admit, I rarely opt for the Deluxe Go Pass, largely because I'm never sure how much time I can dedicate to Go in a month. Nauctis’ First Commander Reveal Has MTG Fans Divided On Its Playability

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's clear that the Magic: The Gathering fan base has already turned its attention firmly to the upcoming launch of Nauctis: The Sunken Realm, following the disappointing reaction to Star Trek.
  • With the confirmation that four Commander precon decks are launching with the set, alongside some very unpopular changes to the Commander precon products, we also had one of the lead Commanders spoiled in the form of a piece of Japanese promo material, and it has led to a rather lengthy debate about whether the assumed lead Commander of the Terrors of the Abyss deck is actually any good.
  • Using machine translation, players were able to get a better look at the Japanese cards leaked via a piece of marketing material that, in all likelihood, wasn't supposed to go live yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's clear that the Magic: The Gathering fan base has already turned its attention firmly to the upcoming launch of Nauctis: The Sunken Realm, following the disappointing reaction to Star Trek.

With the confirmation that four Commander precon decks are launching with the set, alongside some very unpopular changes to the Commander precon products, we also had one of the lead Commanders spoiled in the form of a piece of Japanese promo material, and it has led to a rather lengthy debate about whether the assumed lead Commander of the Terrors of the Abyss deck is actually any good.

Using machine translation, players were able to get a better look at the Japanese cards leaked via a piece of marketing material that, in all likelihood, wasn't supposed to go live yet. In it, we get a look at both Commander options for the Terrors of the Abyss precon, and the presumed lead Commander, The Noble Serpent, is the card at the center of the ongoing debate.

It is an eight-mana (5C, 1B, 1G, 1U) 7/9 and comes with the following rules text: At the beginning of your first upkeep of the game, if The Noble Serpent is in your Command Zone, you mill four cards. At the beginning of your end step, return target creature card that is a Sea Monster from your graveyard to the battlefield.

Sea Monsters are defined as Krakens, Leviathans, Octopuses, Serpents, and Whales, which suggests we could see a lot more of these creature types in the main set for Nauctis, too.

However, players have a problem with the balance of The Noble Serpent and how the card is structured in general. The one-time Eminence ability that triggers at the beginning of your first upkeep is very strange, and it might make more sense to trigger every turn, but for fewer cards. That would then incentivize getting The Noble Serpent onto the battlefield as often as possible, so you can keep digging in your graveyard for creatures to put on the battlefield for free, but there's the risk/reward aspect of not wanting to let them sit in your Command Zone for too long.

The other concern is the creature's cost. At eight mana, it's an expensive Commander, and it feels like its power and toughness could have been lowered to justify knocking a few points off the cost, because the ability to dig through your graveyard once per turn for a free creature is very exciting. While there are easy ways to generate more mana sources early in a game, be it through artifacts or cards in the blue/green card pool, you don't want to compromise the integrity of this deck and restructure its ramp capability just to pay the Commander's cost.

We can see why some players are sold on this card, because it has a really exciting reanimation interaction with your own graveyard and what is sure to be some huge, game-changing creatures, but the cost is a concern, as is the fact that it's the kind of card that just sees you instantly targeted the second it lands on the battlefield because no one wants to deal with what it's capable of.

A quick note on the backup Commander for this deck: it's a four-mana Squid Warlock that gives all creatures Emerge (a mechanic that lets you sacrifice a permanent and use its mana cost towards the casting cost of the spell with Emerge).

GTA 6: How to Find the Secret Satan Boss

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (664 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 has a ton of secrets to find throughout the large map of Leonida.
  • One of the coolest easter eggs in the game is the secret Satan boss fight.
  • If you are looking to take down Satan himself, this guide explains everything you need to know.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 has a ton of secrets to find throughout the large map of Leonida. Some examples include the Kraken deep underwater, UFOs, and even a Mario and Luigi reference.

One of the coolest easter eggs in the game is the secret Satan boss fight. Not only is it a really trippy mission, but it also rewards the player with one of the best weapons in the game.

If you are looking to take down Satan himself, this guide explains everything you need to know. Here’s how to find the secret Satan boss fight in GTA 6.

To find the secret Satan boss in GTA 6, you must travel to the northern side of Port Gellhorn and visit the house with “Welcome to the Hellhole!” written on it. You can find the exact location of this house in the image of Port Gellhorn below.

When you arrive at this house, the garage will either be open or closed. The Satan boss fight event can only be triggered if the garage is open, so if it happens to be shut when you arrive, then you’ll have to come back another time. This event all comes down to RNG, but there are ways to increase your chances.

First, the garage has a higher chance of being open late at night. For example, it was open for me around 10:00 PM, so I recommend only visiting the Hellhole house around this time.

Keep in mind that the event won’t trigger if you just wait outside the house. Instead, I recommend using the RydeMe app to fast travel to another location and back to the house multiple times until the garage opens. This worked for me after five attempts.

In a recent development, once the garage finally opens, walk inside to find two men having some drinks. They will ask you if you want a beer, which you should grab from the cooler next to the couch.

Industry observers note that for the next couple of minutes, make sure you don’t do anything to piss these guys off. You can talk to them, but don’t choose the “provoke” dialogue option or throw a bottle to mess up the event. Instead, wait patiently until their van arrives.

When the van arrives, the men will ask you to join them for their upcoming ritual. You should agree here and climb into the back of the van, which will then transport you to another location with a bonfire.

Next, get out of the van and make your way to the bonfire to celebrate with the two Satanists, and wait until they tell you to look into the fire. Once the prompt “look into the fire” pops up, hold down the button to do just that.

Looking into the fire will teleport you to hell, where you’ll have to fight a wave of Satan’s demons and Satan himself.

Satan is not very difficult to defeat, but the fight can be a bit confusing. What you want to do here is shoot the exploding enemies that are running toward you, which will turn Satan’s health bar red.

In a recent development, once the health bar is red, you want to shoot at Satan to drain his health. When the health bar turns back to black, you want to repeat the process and kill the surrounding enemies to turn the bar red again.

In a recent development, doing this a few times will have Satan going down fairly quickly. Once you kill Satan, you will teleport back to the real world.

When players respawn back to the real world after fighting Satan in GTA 6, they will be granted a permanent health increase. Additionally, they’ll be able to claim the Hellspawn Cumshot 12 Shotgun next to the large throne.

This shotgun is extremely powerful and is one of the best guns I have found in the game so far, so I recommend equipping it for any upcoming missions you have.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that that add-on is All the Things, a must-install for collectors like me, as it acts as a database of all the gear, mounts, titles, crafting recipes, and super rare drops in the game.
  • In a recent development, on occasion, specific items have written notes attached by the All the Things development team, as is true of a special World of Warcraft: Forever toy, the Pouch of Violet Dust.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever there's a whole upcoming world filled with niche gear and strange baubles to collect. But one item in particular has drawn the ire of the creators of a popular completionist add-on.

Industry observers note that that add-on is All the Things, a must-install for collectors like me, as it acts as a database of all the gear, mounts, titles, crafting recipes, and super rare drops in the game. Once you collect something, it is hidden in the add-on, thus tracking your progress and making for a fantastic tool for picking the game apart.

In a recent development, on occasion, specific items have written notes attached by the All the Things development team, as is true of a special World of Warcraft: Forever toy, the Pouch of Violet Dust. This is a promotional item that was obtainable by watching two hours of WoW Forever streams between the 4th and 12th November.

In a recent development, it's a powerful toy! When used on a campfire, it changes the fire's colour to purple and extends the buffs provided by it from the usual one hour to two hours. But the sticking point with the item isn't its existence, rather the fact that it's going to be removed in early December, not long from now.

This is what the creators of the All the Things add-on don't like. "A week-long, Twitch-only window for an item that gets taken away a month later is exactly the kind of FOMO that disheartens collectors," the creators remarked in a note attached to the item in the mod. "It can't be earned by playing the game at all. Even those who get it don't get to keep it.".

It has been revealed that they aren't alone in feeling this way. Comments below the item's listing on the Wowhead database are equally scorching. "I love FOMO in their explicitly non-fomo game," wrote user TheWhiteRose.

Sources indicate that "Just... Why?" added user Darrenic427. "They could very easily just patch out the camp buff duration and keep the visual effect, but Blizzard just doesn't like pretty fire I guess. Figures that they finally give us access to purple fire but then take it away after a month.".

The battle between collectors and time-limited FOMO items is one that has been waged for about as long as these sorts of items have been a part of games. Though for the pouch, it's an especially weird case: an item that's cool to have but so temporary in nature that it makes it both crucial to completionists and strangely pointless to care about. Whether it makes a return in a later patch for World of Warcraft: Forever and doesn't require out-of-game actions to obtain, and doesn't disappear, we'll have to wait and see.

WoW Forever itself is proving popular among players - me included. It's added a staggering amount of fresh quests and many new features to the original version of World of Warcraft, which, in turn, has injected the game with an impressive amount of new items to collect. Completionists will likely be glued to the game for a long time.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The idea of Dark Souls PvP has always scared me a tad.
  • To say that it is just straight up Dark Souls combat would be unfair, from the looks of things.
  • It has been revealed that you can take part in matches with up to eight people, which presumably extends to AI (not that kind) enemies too, in "atmospheric duels, clashes, deathmatches and more." It looks neat!

The idea of Dark Souls PvP has always scared me a tad. You can replace Dark Souls with Bloodborne or Elden Ring, I've typically just been a coward when it comes to the idea of fighting another, real person. They're probably going to be better than me! I don't use tactics in Souls games, I use brute force until I get my way! That being said, I do have to admit I quite like the look of Rasen, a game that is essentially just the PvP component of Dark Souls (or PvE if you just want to take on some computer-controlled enemies) that just rolled out into early access.

To say that it is just straight up Dark Souls combat would be unfair, from the looks of things. For one, it looks more like it leans a tad towards Sekiro with a blades-only kind of affair, whether that be big or small. And blades a plenty they have, ranging from your classic sword, to scythes, to halberds and all sorts. It's a much flashier looking affair too, with fancy slashing effects that seem to buff moves and a pace that seems much faster than Souls games tend to be.

It has been revealed that you can take part in matches with up to eight people, which presumably extends to AI (not that kind) enemies too, in "atmospheric duels, clashes, deathmatches and more." It looks neat! And best of all, unusually for a 3D arena fighter, it has rollback netcode. For those unfamiliar, and to try and explain it simply, this is essentially a bit of tech you'll find in predominantly 2D fighting games that predicts every possible input you could make in a given moment, helping to reduce lag time and allow for tighter matches (and less rage quitting).

That's a bit harder to do in a 3D environment given that you have a lot more options at your disposal when it comes to movement, so if it works that's some impressive stuff! And we could all quite easily find out together, as a demo for Rasen is available to try out. Or, alternatively, you can just pick it up whole hog on Steam right now, as it's available in early access.

Recent findings suggest that unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

As everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the substantial focus of this patch, in case it wasn't obvious.

Industry observers note that the event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

According to recent reports, the hot latest arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this update. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

In combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

It has been revealed that ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

If he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

Recent findings suggest that returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

Version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a fresh activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Rings of Power could have looked very different, according to David Fincher. The Fight Club director claims he was approached about becoming the showrunner of the Lord of the Rings prequel.

Speaking to Josh Horowitz on his Happy Sad Confused podcast, he opened up about navigating interests from streaming services when working creatively, speaking about working on Mindhunter and The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth at Netflix, when he revealed he was also offered The Lord of the Rings show as well.

The Social Network director explained: "I got offered, what is The Lord of the Rings thing at Amazon?" Horowitz replied, "Oh, Rings of Power?" before Fincher revealed: "Oh I got offered that." When quizzed about whether he was approached to just be a director, he explained it was an offer to "showrun" the series.

Sources indicate that "This is before it went to Amazon, and I was like, 'No way', that is an extension of a corporate interest," Fincher continued. "I look at James Gunn and I think, you know, those are bigger balls that I have. I would not want to take on DC and all of its dysfunction." Fincher also revealed in the chat that he had long talks with Kathleen Kennedy about taking on Star Wars too.

It's not clear at what point Fincher was offered the chance to work on what would become The Rings of Power, but given he says it was before it went to Amazon, he was likely involved when the Tolkien Estate was looking at shipping out the television rights for The Lord of the Rings in 2017.

It's reported that Netflix and HBO pitched for this with ideas including a remake of the original trilogy and an Aragorn and Gandalf series. It's possible that Fincher was approached for one of these, but it seems he was out of the conversation before Amazon invited pitches themselves for a fresh story.

Amazon met with the Russo brothers and several other writers before they eventually handed the show to JD Payne and Patrick McKay who are the showrunners of the series today.

For more on The Rings of Power, check out our The Rings of Power season 3 review and our breakdown of The Rings of Power season 3 release schedule.

Recent findings suggest that hoYoverse has delivered another Special Program for the second day running, this time for Zenless Zone Zero. The developer revealed the full details of Version 2.7, subtitled Champions Never Fall to the Past.

This next major update arrives March 24, adding two newly introduced Agents, and introducing the Hollow Champion competition.

Sources indicate that most things in Version 2.7 follow on from the Hollow Champion competition, which brings together old friends and familiar faces, as well interesting newcomers. Everyone is in it to win some massive rewards and earn glory.

Among the unexpected participants the competition has attracted are the Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division, and even some former Calydon's Sweepers. A major challenge that awaits is Black Wolf Romeul, who’s capable of increasing his Crit Damage Resistance and Interruption Resistance by activating a Corruptive Barrier.

Romeul can also cause enemies to continuously lose HP, but you can beat him by putting together a squad that can deal sustained Anomaly damage, which will break through the barrier swiftly.

Our first latest arrival in Version 2.7 is Cissia of the Metropolitan Order Division. She is an S-Rank Electric Attack Agent who automatically gains three stacks of Venom when she enters the battle. Each stack deals Electric Damage while also increasing her Crit Rate for a time.

Recent findings suggest that when she runs out of Venom, which will happen, Cissia can generate more stacks by using her EX Special Attack. She can also use her Basic Attack, Serpent's Kiss, to better utilise the fresh stacks of Venom she generates.

The other new Agent may be the more exciting. Nangong Yu, the captain and lead dancer of the Angels of Delusion, can now be part of your team. Nangong Yu is an S-Rank Ether Stun Agent who can boost her team’s Anomaly Buildup Rate against Stunned enemies.

Recent findings suggest that being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

Returning Agents in Version 2.7 will be Yidhari, the S-Rank Ice Rupture Agent, as well as Seed, the Electric Attack Agent.

Outside of all the very vital action in the core story, this chapter also brings newly introduced themed events to Lumina Square’s Simmer Hot Pot Restaurant. The Simulated Battle Trial is also getting some love, with updated mechanics and new enemy line-ups.

Catch up on our recently updated Zenless Zone Zero character tier list, and don’t forget to check out these Zenless Zone Zero codes before you jump in for some free stuff.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • If a game is about cooking, at minimum I'll have to give it a quick testspin.
  • In a recent development, first up, I just have to gush over the artstyle a bit.
  • I'm also quite pleased about two points made on the game's Steam page.

If a game is about cooking, at minimum I'll have to give it a quick testspin. Outside of this whole writing about video games thing, my other lot in life is soul bound to food, so I'm always curious to see how the two can be mixed together. And earlier this week, The Snackbar at the End of the World was revealed, a wonderfully cartoonish action-adventure game set in a magical, slightly post-apocalyptic version of 1960s Italy where you go out and forage for ingredients while fending off monstrous crops before turning them into tasty meals back in your struggling restaurant.

In a recent development, first up, I just have to gush over the artstyle a bit. The whole game is hand-drawn with a colourful, comic book look that has an impressive sense of depth to it. It gives off a deep love of Italian architecture and landscapes, and that admiration clearly extends to the food too. Once you've gotten the ingredients you need, you then, loosely in the vein of Cooking Mama, prepare them and make various classic Italian dishes by performing some quick minigames. Simple, but charming! The rest of the time you're off killing some ghoulies that look like mutated fruit and veggies, with the occasional fungus-possessed hog and, uh, haunted statues? I think?

I'm also quite pleased about two points made on the game's Steam page. First is the content description: "This game features cartoon violence, sensitive political themes set in a fictional world, and depictions of an oppressive government committing crimes against its citizens." There is clearly a romantic quality to the game and I'd be worried if it didn't acknowledge any of the political context of the decades preceding.

The other line reads, "Every sound effect, musical note, design decision, and line of code is human-made. Because this game is about human relationships and delicious food – and that’s not a story we would ever trust AI to tell." Thank the lord! Right now there's no release date attached to The Snackbar at the End of the World, unsurprising given it was only unveiled this week. But while we all wait for a date, you could perhaps join me in throwing it a wishlist on Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leader of the UK Conservative Party (and former Mortal Kombat player) Kemi Badenoch is more worried about the amount of time people will spend playing GTA 6 rather than the game itself.

Sources indicate that every latest Grand Theft Auto game invites some amount of controversy over its in-game violence or depictions of sex and drugs - from San Andreas' raunchy Hot Coffee mini-game to GTA 5's graphic torture scene. Ahead of GTA 6's release this week, the Tory leader downplayed those fears.

In a recent development, "I would be more worried about the amount of time people were spending on a game than the game specifically. I remember in my childhood playing Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter. I didn't hit anybody after playing those games," Badenoch noted in a news conference shared by Sky News (good spot, IGN).

According to recent reports, while Badenoch's stance might be surprising for the normally right-wing UK political party, she did still worry over children who might play GTA 6 for too long. There are probably far worse ways for kids to spend their time than engaging with a long-form story like GTA 6's, though, especially in an era with endless amounts of 10-second clips to mindlessly scroll past and declining funding into youth programs.

Sources indicate that "I haven't played Grand Theft Auto, I know people are worried about the game content. At the same time, I'd be more worried about a kid who played it all day, who was in their bedroom all day, than one who spends half an hour on it and then went out and did something else. They are two different things," Badenoch added.

GTA 6's release is imminent and is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time. One analyst even suggested GTA 6 could make over $2bn in its opening weekend - that's handily more money than Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey made during its entire run in cinemas, for context.

If you'd like to reminisce a bit before the long-awaited game finally hits, you can check out our favourite Grand Theft Auto pieces Eurogamer's published over the years.

#109946. Exclusive – Behind The Romance: Rockstar Talks GTAVI’s Jason And Lucia

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1568 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gameinformer ↗ Open Full Page

Exclusive – Behind The Romance: Rockstar Talks GTAVI’s Jason And Lucia

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1568 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After dozens of hours exploring Leonida, I have a lot of positive things to say about Grand Theft Auto VI, and shared as much in our review of the game.
  • We reached out to senior members of the Rockstar Games team to ask about their thoughts on Jason and Lucia, and this is what they had to share.
  • During my playthrough, the Jason and Lucia dynamic really elevated the experience, adding heart and emotional weight to the expected mix of action, driving, and activities around Leonida.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After dozens of hours exploring Leonida, I have a lot of positive things to say about Grand Theft Auto VI, and shared as much in our review of the game. But for my part, the feature that elevated the game most prominently above Rockstar Games’ other (excellent) games wasn’t its graphics, missions, or action – it was the storytelling and interplay between the two lead protagonists. Jason and Lucia bring heart, emotional depth, and a sense of genuine threat to the crime fantasy, as you grow attached to them and start cheering for them against all the odds stacked against them.

We reached out to senior members of the Rockstar Games team to ask about their thoughts on Jason and Lucia, and this is what they had to share.

During my playthrough, the Jason and Lucia dynamic really elevated the experience, adding heart and emotional weight to the expected mix of action, driving, and activities around Leonida. Was a couple or romantic relationship the plan or goal for the game from very early on in development, or did that come later? Do you see the focus on Jason and Lucia’s relationship as one of the features that separates Grand Theft Auto VI from your prior work on storytelling in the game series?

Industry observers note that stephen Donkin, Vice President of Design: “The dual protagonists and the relationship between the two of them was there from very early in development, but exactly how that was expressed in the game did change over time. It was an enormous challenge for us to get them working together in the open world together and finding exactly how that would work. As we started to layer in more mechanics, dialogue, and incremental features across all teams, it just clicked at some point. The ability to be together in the open world also allowed us for new ways to tell the story of the game and to bring some of the exposition and narrative into the open world in a way we hadn’t been able to do before. Hearing these little bits of dialogue as you are just tooling around the world that have specific context to what you as a player have just been doing in the story really knits it all together.”.

The player has a choice for how to develop the relationship between the two leads, but I imagine most players are drawn toward helping it thrive. In early playtests, is that what you observed?

Katie Pica, Design Director: Player Systems & Progression:“Overall, we’ve seen that players are invested in supporting Jason and Lucia’s relationship but we don’t favor a specific path through the game, it is completely down to player choice.”.

Industry observers note that it feels like a lot of the game’s driving narrative beats factor for a close connection between Jason and Lucia. Was it challenging to craft variations that included a more tense or distant connection between the two? Is that even possible?

Luke Howard, Senior Design Director: Missions & Visualization:“One of the core goals of this game was to tell the story of Jason and Lucia with a base line relationship where they are amicable, if just platonic, as they still share the same ultimate goals and need each other to achieve them. So, this gave us a good platform on the main flow to expand particularly intense or emotional moments they experience with variation that can expand on their romantic relationship, while not losing anything if that doesn’t exist. In short, we did develop variation in scenes and interactions that range from subtle to more significant, but done in a way that should feel authentic to the player’s choices, relationship-wise and also criminal profile.

Industry observers note that one example is after Lucia helps Kordell’s gang pull off an intense armored truck robbery she shares the information with Raul’s crew. Afterwards Jason pulls Lucia aside to see how she's coping. This moment carries several variations where the performance direction was captured multiple ways to cover a range emotional energy between them. The actors deliveries are brilliant and nuanced – these small tender moments are where we tried to craft pieces that when added up together over the course of the story, author an authentic version of the player’s Jason and Lucia.”.

Were there any fictional couples or real-life couples that the team looked at for inspiration in shaping the Jason and Lucia dynamic, whether those couples came from massive crime stories or not?

In a recent development, rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“We definitely started by looking at all the “couple on the run” movies. There are a lot of them but the ones that we kept coming back to were Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway in Bonnie and Clyde, McQueen and MacGraw in The Getaway (the Jim Thomson book is also great), True Romance, Thelma and Louise. Clooney and JLo’s dynamic in Out of Sight, as well. And then a lot of buddy movies actually – Riggs and Murtaugh, Butch and Sundance, Mike Lowry and Marcus Burnett, etc. for their back and forth together. In terms of having a game where the characters can change based on how you play and whether you really lean into and enjoy the crime spree we thought about how both Pulp Fiction and Natural Born Killers start with a couple in a diner pulling out guns, but then how different those couples are and how different those scenarios play out. Jason and Lucia are a lot tougher than Tim Roth and Amanda Plummer but we liked the idea of telling a story where Jason and Lucia could end up being closer to either end of that spectrum based on what the player was doing.”.

Industry observers note that sex and intimacy are notoriously complicated and challenging to present in games. How did you aim to strike a balance with their private moments together that felt authentic? Any thoughts about how or why it’s so challenging to present adult relationships in video games?

In a recent development, rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“This is definitely something we thought a lot about and spent a long time trying to get right. The actors who play Jason and Lucia were so good, and they had a natural chemistry and part of it was just trying to capture some of that.

Sources indicate that there’s this trade off in making games between player control and then scripted scenarios. We try and give the player as much control as we can because we are working in an interactive medium and actually doing something rather than watching it is going to feel more powerful. But then you have the ability to really mess around and break the illusion of a tender or romantic moment or whatever it is. So the relationship aspect of this story is there if a player wants to engage in it, but if they don’t the story can play out differently.”.

In its best moments of genuine support, regular connection, open communication, and flirty or engagement with one another, Jason and Lucia can come across as a pretty ideal model of good relationships – even while they’re simultaneously committing major crimes together. Was that juxtaposition of a healthy romantic relationship against an external world of illicit activity an explicit goal for how the narrative came together?

Rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“That was the goal, yes. You are really living with these characters – they’re eating, sleeping, showering, throwing away their trash, or not. The relationship needed to feel real to sit alongside all of that. Then even just as a development team, we live with these characters for years and years. We wanted them to be people we could like, care about, and root for. And they needed to like each other. But then the world itself is so crazy and chaotic and seemingly on the brink of collapse.

When we set out to make this game, and go into that multiyear development marathon, we said we wanted to spend our time working on something with heart, and with some characters you could care about and root for. It’s barely worth even stating, but we are living in a time when people are divided along almost every line, and feelings about the future are pretty bleak. We wanted to create a world that held up a mirror to that, indicated that fever pitch of craziness that we are all maybe a couple of bad decisions away from, but we wanted the story we were going to tell to have something positive at its core and the message that human connection is better than division.”.

In a recent development, the game automatically moves you to play one character or another at certain points, but for many sequences, you can choose your playable lead. In your experience playing and watching others play, do most players gravitate toward one character or another as “their character?”.

Stephen Donkin, Vice President of Design:“It really varied in our playthroughs. They are both such great characters and performances that people seemed to gravitate to both of them in different ways. But overall, we have found the split of time between characters to be relatively even on a per-playthrough and also at a macro level.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has been out in the hands of console players for a few days now, and a few of us at PC Gamer have been dusting off our PlayStations and Xboxes to dive into Leonida as we eagerly anticipate its eventual (but yet unannounced) PC release next year potentially.

Recent findings suggest that I've been gaming it up myself and, as is always the case with GTA, I am absolutely loving driving around. Flying down the highway, exploring all the alleyways and retail areas, and taking out to the waters on a boat or jetski. All of it, of course, to the soundtrack of GTA 6's various radio stations.

Recent findings suggest that there are a huge number of stations in this game—19 of them, to be exact—with a ton of excellently-curated songs lingering within and famous cameo hosts. Usually I find myself just picking one station and sticking to it, but with GTA 6? I've been cycling between quite a few, each one offering something a little bit different.

Four stations have been grabbing most of my attention though. Pop station Flash FM has easily gained the most airtime in my playthrough so far. Am I listening to Ariana Grande in my everyday life? No. But am I bombing it down the highway while singing Break Free to myself every time it comes on? I absolutely am.

According to recent reports, but I've also been peppering in a ton of 80s station Vice City FM. I mean, c'mon, you've got Weird Al Yankovic as a co-host, first of all. But you've also got straight up bangers like Lionel Richie's All Night Long, Simply Red's Money's Too Tight (To Mention), and Billy Ocean's Loverboy.

Industry observers note that there's also Emotion 98.3, the radio station dedicated to songs about love (both being in love and being heartbroken, of course) and yes, I have stayed in the car waiting to hear Phil Collins' excellent drumming in In The Air Tonight. And finally, because I am a raging emo at heart, I've obviously had to whack on a bunch of The Chamber 106.6. Tool, System of a Down, and Metallica? Count me in.

But what about you? If any of you PC gamers are partaking on console, is only one radio station catching your attention, or have you found yourself channel hopping just like me? Or is there somehow not a single station that's caught your fancy, instead finding the podcasts a more entertaining use of your listening time? Be sure to drop a comment and let me know.

You can't beat the classics, and Joytoy's standard Intercessors are all incredibly well done. Only the White Scars version is on offer right now, but that just gives me an excuse to praise a faction I think is critically underrated.

Elsewhere in the hobby, these new Bretonnia models imply just how successful Warhammer The Old World has become.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, while following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying half-hidden among ivy and moss.
  • You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon.
  • As you step forward, your toe nudges an ornamental scroll.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, while following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying half-hidden among ivy and moss. Scraping away the dirt, you discover a faint, absurd engraving of a newspaper. What mystery is here? You turn the brass knob – strange, it is warm! – and the engraving of the newspaper flutters. The pages turn faster and faster, emitting a howling gale that bowls you head over foot. When you pick yourself up, you are inside a vast attic full of books and bricabrac, lit from one side by windows that offer no view of the outside world – just light and mist.

Tarnation! You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon. Fortunately, there are several ways to escape. Each of the arcane objects before you is secretly a portal, transporting you to another site of arcane activity, in a bizarre web of diversions that cannot possibly reflect the hand of a human curator. Which will you choose?

As you step forward, your toe nudges an ornamental scroll. It growls and wriggles like a panicking caterpillar, scooting away under a table. Before you lose sight of it, you discern the title and subject of the text – it's an essay by Kyle Tam about the yokai of Promise Mascot Agency.

Sources indicate that deep in a drawer, you discover a sour-smelling binder full of extracts from an ancient and all but indecipherable dispute over the discovery of "generative AI" in something called "Big Walk". The stakes are long-buried, but many of the individual pieces of writing are lively. Here is Bruno Dias noting in passing that "one of the harms of the 'AI' political project is the propaganda machine dedicated to making you feel stupid and helpless." Here is a professorial interjection from Brendan Keogh calling on the warring parties to recognise when "critiques of generative AI are actually just deflected critiques of the capitalist relations of technology and labour". Here is Mike Cook arguing that "what's happening is not unusual, it's not extreme, it's not unfair and it's not a 'public flogging'." Here is a ticker tape message from Hannah Nicklin observing that "if your radical position doesn’t have room for transformation it will not be safe until it contains just you".

A footnote in the same dusty sheaf of papers points you towards another work from Mike Cook in a different drawer. This one consists of neon slides, slotted into an antique View-Master, and explores a comparison between procedural generation and street photography.

Sources indicate that peering at the weirdly white and opaque windowpanes, you realise there are intricate equations traced in the condensation. It appears to be a post-mortem for a "post-cosy" game called Danchi Days, in which developer Melos Han-Tani discusses wishlist conversion rates and the problem of not fitting neatly into any recognisable genre.

Sources indicate that A snowglobe stands on a mantelpiece, the flakes still orbiting a miniature washtub as though the object had been recently shaken, even though the chamber has clearly been abandoned for decades. You put it to your ear, anticipating the faint jingle of Xmas bells. Instead, you are almost deafened by a screeching guitar chord. Here is Erin Keane to explain.

Next to the snowglobe on the mantelpiece, there's a souvenir shop conch shell, polished to a high sheen. You put that to your ear, hoping to catch the soothing shuffle of surf on shingle, and a disembodied voice tells you to piss off. Tim Sniffen has some thoughts about gentrification, and why only he should be allowed to do it.

It has been revealed that again, one of these mystic artefacts hides the key to your release from the suffocating stillness of Sunday Afternoon. Which will you choose? Or have you, perhaps, brought a sorcerous teleportation device of your own? Please share. Here is Joanna Newsom's Cosmia to help you think.

Original GTA 6 leaker pleads guilty to hacking Rockstar Games, years after first revealing Lucia

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The 21-year-old responsible for hacking Rockstar Games and leaking in-development GTA 6 footage in 2022 has pleaded guilty to a number of offenses.
  • Sources indicate that the GTA 6 leaker was initially sentenced to an indefinite stay at a hospital due to his severe autism, but was more recently deemed fit for trial and moved to a regular prison earlier this January.
  • At the time of his Rockstar hack - when he was between the ages of 16 and 17 - the leaker was already under police protection at a Travelodge hotel to keep him from rival hackers he had allegedly stolen Bitcoin from.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 21-year-old responsible for hacking Rockstar Games and leaking in-development GTA 6 footage in 2022 has pleaded guilty to a number of offenses.

Sources indicate that the GTA 6 leaker was initially sentenced to an indefinite stay at a hospital due to his severe autism, but was more recently deemed fit for trial and moved to a regular prison earlier this January. On Monday, at the Woolwich Crown Court in South East London, he pleaded guilty to hacking Rockstar Games and a number of other companies, including Uber and EE/BT, in cyber attacks estimated to have caused £10m in damages.

At the time of his Rockstar hack - when he was between the ages of 16 and 17 - the leaker was already under police protection at a Travelodge hotel to keep him from rival hackers he had allegedly stolen Bitcoin from. Somewhat surprisingly, he then managed to hack the multi-billion dollar game maker with nothing but an Amazon Fire Stick, the hotel room's TV and a bluetooth-connected keyboard and mouse.

Sources indicate that as the BBC reports, he also managed to break into the developer's Slack channels, before threatening to release the GTA 6 source code if Rockstar failed to contact him within the day. The leaker has yet to be sentenced.

Those 2022 leaks were quite substantial, too, revealing about an hour of unfinished gameplay and clueing the world in on Lucia's existence - the series' first female protagonist in years. Of course, those 2022 leaks shouldn't be confused with 2026's, which saw Cyberleek spill nuggets of nearly finished clips onto the internet, despite Rockstar's best efforts to keep GTA 6 a closely guarded secret.

Recent findings suggest that "We recently suffered a network intrusion in which an unauthorised third-party illegally accessed and downloaded confidential information from our systems, including early development footage for the next Grand Theft Auto," Rockstar said at the time, before it had officially unveiled GTA 6. "At this time we do not anticipate any disruption to our live game services, nor any long-term effect on the development of our ongoing projects. We are extremely disappointed to have any details of our next game shared with you all in this way.".

Four years later, GTA 6 is finally around the corner - you're probably already aware considering the marketing frenzy Rockstar's been drumming up.
